1:1.headline: Cyrus, כורש, read as כשר, 'fit', with letters swapped
1:1.body: Ibn Ezra reports that some see in כורש the word כשר, 'fit' or 'worthy', with its letters turned around. They say Isaiah named him for the good he would do for Israel.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: שהמלה נהפכת מן וכשר הדבר כי כבר כנהו בשמו הנביא ישעיהו על הכשרון שיעשה עם ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some say the name is כשר turned around, given by Isaiah for the good Cyrus would do for Israel.

1:1.headline: Jeremiah's word fulfilled, or Jeremiah's prophecy ended?
1:1.body: Rashi reads לכלות as 'to complete': the seventy years Jeremiah foretold were up. Maimonides cites this verse to show that prophecy left Jeremiah before he died.

sources.quote: לִזְמַן אֲשֶׁר הֻשְׁלַם דְּבָרוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר יִרְמְיָהוּ הַנָּבִיא
sources.says: Rashi says it means at the time when God's word, spoken by Jeremiah, was completed.

sources.quote: כי אין מנוס מהסתלקות הנבואה משאר הנביאים (מלבד משה) לפני מותם, בפרק זמן קצר או ארוך, כמו שהתבאר על ירמיה
sources.says: Maimonides says prophecy leaves every prophet but Moses before death, as this verse shows for Jeremiah.

1:2.headline: Why Cyrus says 'God of heaven' and not 'of the earth'
1:2.body: Ibn Ezra says Cyrus left out the earth because it was given to people to run. Malbim says Cyrus thought God hands the earth to a ruler he chooses, and saw himself as that ruler.

sources.quote: אלהי השמים - ולא אמר אלהי הארץ כי כבר נתנה לבני אדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he did not say 'God of the earth' because the earth was already given to people.

sources.quote: וקראו רק אלהי השמים כי חשב שהנהגת הארץ ימסור ביד מי שיתמנה להיות במקומו
sources.says: Malbim says Cyrus called him only God of heaven because he thought God hands rule of the earth to one he appoints in his place.

1:4.headline: 'Whoever remains': the poor who can't go, or those who stay?
1:4.body: Rashi says הנשאר is the Jew left behind for lack of money, and his neighbors must pay his way. Ralbag reads it the other way: the Jews who stay behind must help those who go.

sources.quote: וְכָל יְהוּדִי הַנִּשְׁאָר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת מֵחֲמַת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָמוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means any Jew who stays in place because he has no money to go up.

sources.quote: וכל הנשאר - שהוא דל ואין ידו משגת ממון לעלות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra agrees: the one who remains is poor and cannot afford to go up.

sources.quote: שאשר ישאר מישראל מכל המקומות אשר גר שם העולה לירושלים לבנות את בית ה' ינשאו כל אחד מהעולים
sources.says: Ralbag says those of Israel who remain in each place should support each person going up to Jerusalem.

1:4.headline: ינשאוהו: give him gifts, or lift him up?
1:4.body: נשא can mean to carry gifts or to raise up. Ibn Ezra prefers 'lift him up', since the poor man is low, and Malbim adds that it also means lifting his spirit.

sources.quote: ינשאוהו - יתנו לו משאות ומתנות, או ינשאוהו ירימוהו מענין רם ונשא, כי העני בשפל והוא הנכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means either 'give him gifts' or 'raise him up', and prefers the second, because the poor man is low.

sources.quote: שינשאוהו שכולל שינשאו את רוחו לזה
sources.says: Malbim says the word also includes lifting his spirit for the task.

1:8.headline: Sheshbazzar: 'six troubles', or Zerubbabel's foreign name?
1:8.body: The sages say Sheshbazzar is Daniel, named for the six troubles (שש צרות) he lived through. Ibn Ezra, Ralbag and Metzudat David say he is Zerubbabel, called by his Babylonian or Persian name.

sources.quote: הוּא שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר הוּא דָנִיֵּאל, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר? שֶׁעָמַד בְּשֵׁשׁ צָרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages that Sheshbazzar is Daniel, so called because he stood through six troubles.

sources.quote: לששבצר - הוא זרובבל ונקרא כן בלשון כשדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he is Zerubbabel, called this in the Chaldean language.

sources.quote: והוא זרובבל וכן היה נקרא בל׳ פרס
sources.says: Metzudat David says he is Zerubbabel, called this in Persian, and also cites the sages' view.

1:9.headline: אגרטלי: bowls that 'gather' the lamb's blood
1:9.body: אגרטלי is a rare word for Temple vessels. Ibn Ezra cites the Jerusalem Talmud, which hears in it אוגרים, 'gather', and טלה, 'lamb': bowls that collect the lamb's blood.

sources.quote: ופירושו בירושלמי: למה נקרא שמם אגרטלי? שאוגרים שם דם הטלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the Jerusalem Talmud: they are called אגרטלי because the lamb's blood is gathered in them.

sources.quote: אגרטלי - המלה חמישית או הא' נוסף ופירושו גביעים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra also says it may be a five-letter word, or the א is added, and that it means cups.

1:9.headline: מחלפים: knives, named for 'changing' life to death
1:9.body: מחלפים means knives. Metzudat Zion says the name comes from חלף, 'pass away', because they turn the living into the dead, and Rashi links it to the Temple room where knives were kept.

sources.quote: ע״ש שבהם שוחטים ומחליפים מחיים למיתה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are named so because with them one slaughters and changes life into death.

sources.quote: מַחֲלָפִים. הֵם סַכִּינִים, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן בֵּית הַחֲלָפוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they are knives, named like the Temple chamber of החליפות where knives were placed.

sources.quote: מחלפים. סכינים והוא מענין כליל יחלוף, בני חלוף, שטעמם כריתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are knives, from חלף, which means cutting off.

1:10.headline: כפורי: basins named for 'wiping' off the blood
1:10.body: כפורי are basins for the blood of offerings. Rashi says the name means 'wiping', because the priest wiped blood drops from his hand on the basin's rim.

sources.quote: מִזְרָקִים, וְנִקְרְאוּ כְּפוֹרֵי מִלְּשׁוֹן קִנּוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says they are basins, called כפורי from a word for wiping.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַבֵּל דָּם בַּמִּזְרָק הָיָה מְקַנֵּחַ נִצּוֹצוֹת הַדָּם שֶׁנִּתְּזוּ עַל יָדוֹ בִּשְׂפַת הַמִּזְרָק
sources.says: Rashi says the priest catching the blood wiped the splashed drops off his hand on the basin's rim.

sources.quote: לזה קרוי כפור שהוא ענין קנוח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion gives the same reason: כפור means wiping.

1:10.headline: משנים: second-rank basins, or double-sided ones?
1:10.body: משנים comes from 'two' or 'second'. Malbim and Ibn Ezra read it as second in rank, after the gold ones, while Metzudat Zion reads it as double, usable from both sides.

sources.quote: משנים, שהיו אחרי הקודמים במדרגה
sources.says: Malbim says they ranked below the ones listed before.

sources.quote: משנים - לכפורי זהב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they were second to the gold basins.

sources.quote: משנים. מל׳ שניים ור״ל כפולים הראוי להשתמש בהן בשתי עבריהן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means doubled, usable on both sides.

2:1.headline: 'The province': the land of Israel, or Babylon?
2:1.body: Rashi says the province is the land of Israel, which these exiles came from. Ibn Ezra says it is the province of Babylon.

sources.quote: אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר מִמְּדִינַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says these are the Israelites from the province of the land of Israel, now coming up from captivity.

sources.quote: בני המדינה - היא מדינת בבל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the province is the province of Babylon.

2:2.headline: Mordecai 'Bilshan': the man who knew many languages
2:2.body: Metzudat David cites the sages: Bilshan is part of the name of Mordecai of the Esther story, given because he knew seventy languages (לשון). Ibn Ezra agrees this is that Mordecai but thinks Bilshan may be a separate man.

sources.quote: מרדכי בלשן. הוא שם אחד והוא דוד לאסתר המלכה ונקרא בלשן על שידע בשבעים לשון
sources.says: Metzudat David says Mordecai Bilshan is one name, the relative of Queen Esther, called Bilshan because he knew seventy languages, as the sages say.

sources.quote: מרדכי שידע כמה לשונות
sources.says: Malbim says that in the sages' view it is one name, Mordecai who knew many languages, while some take it as two names.

sources.quote: הוא מרדכי היהודי. רק בלשן יתכן שהוא איש אחר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this is Mordecai the Jew, but Bilshan may be another man.

2:2.headline: The same letters twice: once a man's name, once 'the count'
2:2.body: מספר appears twice in this verse. Rashi says the first, with a long vowel, is the name of one of the leaders, and the second means 'the number' of the people.

sources.quote: הָרִאשׁוֹן פּ״א קְמוּצָה בְּגָדוֹל וְשֵׁם אָדָם הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the first מספר has a long a-vowel under the פ and is a person's name, while the second has a short vowel and means 'the number of'.

sources.quote: מספר - השני בפסוק הוא שם חשבון והראשון שם איש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the second מספר means a count and the first is a man's name.

2:43.headline: The Netinim are 'the given ones', the Gibeonites Joshua assigned
2:43.body: נתינים means 'given'. Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra say they were the Gibeonites, whom Joshua gave to cut wood and draw water for the house of God, and the name stuck.

sources.quote: הם הגבעונים ונקראו נתינים ע״ש שנאמר בם ויתנם יהושע חוטבי עצים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the Gibeonites, called נתינים because it says 'Joshua gave them as woodcutters'.

sources.quote: נְתִינִים שֶׁהָיוּ חוֹטְבֵי עֵצִים וְשׁוֹאֲבֵי מַיִם לָעֵדָה
sources.says: Rashi says the Netinim were the woodcutters and water-drawers for the community.

sources.quote: ויהושע נתנם לבית אלהיו, ועל כן נקראו נתינים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Joshua gave them to the house of his God, and so they were called נתינים.

2:61.headline: Priests who took their wife's family name, and lost their proof
2:61.body: These priests were called 'sons of Barzillai' after Barzillai of Gilead, whose daughter their ancestor married. Malbim says the borrowed name later raised doubt about whether they were priests at all.

sources.quote: וְהָיָה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל בַּרְזִלַּי עַל שְׁמָם, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם לָקְחוּ מִבְּנוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says Barzillai's name was called on them because they married his daughters.

sources.quote: על שם הבנות שהם מזרע ברזילי, קרא את שם עצמו ברזילי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he called himself Barzillai after his wife, a descendant of Barzillai.

sources.quote: כי יש לחוש שאינם כהנים כלל רק ישראלים מבני ברזילי
sources.says: Malbim says there was a worry that they were not priests at all, but ordinary Israelites from a family called Barzillai.

2:62.headline: Treated as 'soiled' and removed from the priesthood
2:62.body: ויגאלו means they were made unclean, like the 'polluted bread' in Malachi. Rashi says they were treated as defiled and could no longer serve with the other priests, because their family record was not found.

sources.quote: ויגואלו. ענין טנוף ונמאס כמו לחם מגואל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means soiled and rejected, as in 'polluted bread'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ מְגֹאָלִים וּמְגֹעָלִים שֶׁלֹּא יַעַבְדוּ עוֹד עִם שְׁאָר הַכֹּהֲנִים
sources.says: Rashi says they were treated as defiled and rejected, so they would no longer serve with the other priests.

sources.quote: מלשון לחם מגואל. והטעם: נמאסו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is like 'polluted bread' and means they were rejected.

2:63.headline: Tirshatha: 'permitted to drink', or a foreign title?
2:63.body: Rashi and Metzudat David cite the sages: Nehemiah was called התרשתא, read as התר שתא, 'permitted to drink', because as the king's cupbearer he was allowed gentile wine. Ibn Ezra prefers to read it as a title of rank in the Chaldean language, like 'officer' or 'governor'.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ הַתִּרְשָׁתָא שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לִשְׁתּוֹת יֵין נֶסֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: he was called Tirshatha because the sages permitted him to drink gentile wine, since he served drinks to the king.

sources.quote: והיא מלה מורכבת התר שתא
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a compound word: התר שתא, permitted to drink.

sources.quote: ויתכן: שהוא שם תפארת וגדולה בלשון כשדים, כעניין שר או פחה והוא הנכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the drinking explanation but says the right one is a title of honor in Chaldean, like officer or governor.

4:2.headline: Written 'not', read 'to him': two ways to hear their offer
4:2.body: The written text has ולא, 'not', but it is read ולו, 'to him'. Read aloud, the neighbors claim they sacrifice to Israel's God; Ibn Ezra reads the written form as 'we sacrifice to no other'.

sources.quote: קרי בוי"ו וכתיב באל"ף, ופירש ולא אנחנו זובחים לזולתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes the word is read with vav and written with aleph, and explains: we sacrifice to no other.

sources.quote: הכותים היו עובדים בשיתוף
sources.says: Malbim says these settlers worshipped God alongside other gods, and thought Israel did the same.

4:3.headline: Here כי means 'rather', not 'because'
4:3.body: כי usually means 'because' or 'that'. Rashi says here it stands for אלא, 'rather': not you and us, rather we alone will build.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא אֲנַחְנוּ לְבַדֵּנוּ נִבְנֶה כִּי זֶה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּמְקוֹם אֶלָּא
sources.says: Rashi says כי here is used in place of אלא, 'rather': we alone will build.

4:4.headline: Spelled as 'terrors', read as 'frightening'
4:4.body: The written word swaps two letters, as if it came from בלהות, terrors. It is read מבהלים, frightening, and Ibn Ezra says both roots mean the same.

sources.quote: ומבלהים - כתיב מן בלהות אתנך, ומבהלים קרי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the written form comes from בלהות, terrors, the read form from בהל, and the meaning is the same.

4:4.headline: 'To build' here means 'from building'
4:4.body: The neighbors frightened the Jews 'to build', which sounds backwards. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means 'from building', like 'he stopped counting' in Genesis 41.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ מִלִּבְנוֹת, וְכֵן ״עַד כִּי חָדַל לִסְפֹּר״
sources.says: Rashi says לבנות means 'from building', as in 'until he stopped counting'.

sources.quote: לבנות. כמו מלבנות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'from building'.

4:6.headline: A letter of accusation, from שטן, the adversary
4:6.body: שטנה appears only here. Ibn Ezra reads it from שטן, to oppose, and Metzudat Zion calls it an accusation.

sources.quote: כתבו שטנה - מן שטן, והטעם לסטון אותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from שטן, and means a letter written to oppose them.

sources.quote: שטנה. ענין קטרוג
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means accusation.

4:7.headline: One king, three names: Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes
4:7.body: Rashi says this Artaxerxes is Cyrus, and quotes the Talmud: he was called Cyrus because he was a worthy (כשר) king, and Artaxerxes after his kingdom. Metzudat David says Artaxerxes was a title for every Persian king, like Pharaoh in Egypt.

sources.quote: כּוֹרֶשׁ עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ כָּשֵׁר הָיָה, אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׂתָּא עַל שֵׁם הַמַּלְכוּת
sources.says: Rashi says Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes are one king; Cyrus because he was a worthy king, Artaxerxes for the kingdom.

sources.quote: ושם ארתחששתא הוא כנוי לכל מלכי פרס כמו פרעה למצרים
sources.says: Metzudat David says Artaxerxes is a title for all Persian kings, like Pharaoh for Egypt.

4:7.headline: 'In peace', or the name of a man?
4:7.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read בשלם as 'in peace': the letter was written in friendly words. Malbim reads it as a name, one of the men who wrote the letter.

sources.quote: כָּתַב מִכְתָּבוֹ בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says he wrote his letter in words of peace.

sources.quote: כתב בשלם - כמו בשלום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בשלם means 'in peace'.

sources.quote: תחלה אמר שהכותבים היו בשלם מתרדת
sources.says: Malbim treats בשלם as one of the writers, named together with מתרדת.

4:7.headline: Aramaic letters, and the Aramaic language too
4:7.body: ומתרגם appears only here and means set out or expressed. Rashi says the letter used Aramaic script and was also expressed in the Aramaic language.

sources.quote: הַמִּכְתָּב הָיָה מְפֹרָשׁ בְּלָשׁוֹן אֲרָמִית
sources.says: Rashi says the letter was set out in the Aramaic language, after saying it was in Aramaic letters.

sources.quote: ומתרגם. גם הוא ענין מפורש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'set out clearly', and cites the sages' use of the word.

4:8.headline: The scribe Shimshai, said to be Haman's son
4:8.body: Rashi says Shimshai the scribe was a son of Haman. He adds that the Bible often names a scribe and a recorder together, since each needs the other.

sources.quote: הוּא שִׁמְשַׁי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל הָמָן
sources.says: Rashi says this Shimshai is the son of Haman.

4:8.headline: 'Master of taste': the man skilled in counsel and words
4:8.body: טעם means taste, but here it means skill with counsel and words. Ibn Ezra ties it to 'taste and see' in Psalm 34, and Metzudat Zion to 'the judgment of elders' in Job 12.

sources.quote: מן טעמו וראו, והנה רחום בעל טעם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from 'taste and see', and here means counsel.

sources.quote: ענינו היודע מיטב הדבור במליצה נאותה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means one who knows how to put words well.

4:8.headline: A letter, named for gathering many words together
4:8.body: Metzudat Zion says a sent letter is called אגרה because many things are gathered into it. He ties it to אוגר, 'gathers', in Proverbs 10.

sources.quote: ע״ש שמאוסף בו דברים הרבה והוא מל׳ אוגר בקיץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the letter is named for the many things gathered in it, from 'gathers in summer'.

4:10.headline: Osnappar is Sennacherib under another name
4:10.body: Rashi says Osnappar, who moved foreign peoples into Samaria, is Sennacherib. Metzudat David adds that Osnappar is his name in Persian.

sources.quote: אָסְנַפַּר. סַנְחֵרִיב
sources.says: Rashi says Osnappar is Sennacherib.

sources.quote: אשר הגלה אסנפר והוא סנחריב בלשון פרסי
sources.says: Metzudat David says Osnappar is Sennacherib's name in Persian.

4:12.headline: Building the Temple, or the city? A trick of wording
4:12.body: Malbim says the phrase can mean they are building the Temple in a rebel city, or they are building the rebel city itself. The accusers used wording that sounded like the second but could be defended as the first.

sources.quote: כי בלשון זה יש שני פירושים
sources.says: Malbim says this wording has two readings, and the copyists used it to deceive the king.

4:13.headline: Not 'and went', but a toll on the king's road
4:13.body: הלך usually means walking. Here it names a tax: Ibn Ezra says a toll on those who travel the king's road, and Metzudat Zion says a gift brought when the king passes through.

sources.quote: והלך - מכס ההולכים דרך המלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הלך is the toll paid by those who travel the king's road.

sources.quote: הוא תשודה המביאים למלך בעת יעבור אליהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a gift brought to the king when he passes by.

4:14.headline: Not fitting for us, or we will not wait?
4:14.body: Rashi reads אריך as 'fitting', a word the Talmud uses in Sukkah. Ibn Ezra reads it as 'wait', from the Aramaic for 'he waited': we will not wait to see the king shamed.

sources.quote: אֲרִיךְ הָגוּן כְּמוֹ ״אֲרִיךְ אוֹ לָא אֲרִיךְ״ בְּמַסֶּכֶת סֻכָּה
sources.says: Rashi says אריך means fitting, as the Talmud uses it in tractate Sukkah.

sources.quote: וערות המלך וגנותו לא נוחיל לראות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads it from the Aramaic for 'wait': we will not wait to see the king's shame.

4:15.headline: Revolt, from a word for sending messengers
4:15.body: Metzudat Zion reads ואשתדור as revolt, from שדר, 'to send', since rebels send messengers to ask for help. Malbim links it instead to משתדר in Daniel 6:15, making an effort.

sources.quote: והוא מלשון שדר שהוא שליחות בלשון ארמי כי כן דרך המורדים לשלוח שלוחים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from שדר, sending, because rebels send messengers to get help.

sources.quote: תרגום הנה שלחתי את הגדי הזה שדרית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra ties it to the Aramaic שדרית, 'I sent'.

sources.quote: ואשתדור כמו ואשתדל כמו בדניאל
sources.says: Malbim says it means effort, like the word in Daniel 6.

4:17.headline: A place, a greeting of peace, or a scribe's 'etc.'?
4:17.body: Rashi reads שלם as a place name, and Metzudat David as a greeting of peace. Malbim reads it as a scribe's shorthand for 'and the rest', like our 'etc.'.

sources.quote: שְׁלָם וּכְעֶת. מְקוֹמוֹת הֵם
sources.says: Rashi says שלם and כעת are places.

sources.quote: לכולם יהיה שלום וגם לכעת יהיה שלום
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a greeting: peace to all of them.

sources.quote: שלם, פי' והשלם וגמור יתר הדברים עד וכענת, והוא כמו מלת וכו'
sources.says: Malbim says שלם means 'complete the rest of the names', like our 'etc.'.

5:1.headline: 'Son of Iddo' here means his grandson
5:1.body: Zechariah is called בר עדוא, son of Iddo. Malbim says בר here means grandson.

sources.quote: בר עדוא ר"ל בן בנו
sources.says: Malbim says 'son of Iddo' means Iddo's grandson.

5:3.headline: A rare word for walls, with two guesses at its root
5:3.body: ואשרנא means the walls. Rashi, following Menachem, links it to אשיא, foundations; Ibn Ezra takes it from שור, wall, with an extra א in front.

sources.quote: הַכְּתָלִים הָאֵלֶּה לְיַסֵּד, כְּמוֹ ״וְאֻשַּׁיָּא יְחִיטוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means these walls, like ואשיא in Ezra 4:12, as Menachem grouped it.

sources.quote: ואושרנא - מן אדלג שור והאל"ף נוסף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from שור, wall, as in 'I leap over a wall', with an added aleph.

5:4.headline: Who is the 'we' who said this?
5:4.body: The verse suddenly says 'we told them'. Ibn Ezra says it is the builders or the scribes speaking, Metzudat David says the book's author, and Malbim says the builders telling the story.

sources.quote: הם דברי הבונים, או דברי הסופרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these are the words of the builders, or of the scribes.

sources.quote: זה מדברי כותב הספר
sources.says: Metzudat David says these are the words of the book's writer.

sources.quote: ויספרו הבונים כדברים האלה אמרנו להם
sources.says: Malbim says the builders are telling what they said.

5:14.headline: Who was Sheshbazzar: Daniel or Zerubbabel?
5:14.body: Rashi says Sheshbazzar is Daniel. Ralbag and Ibn Ezra say he is Zerubbabel, and Ibn Ezra gives two proofs.

sources.quote: לְיַד שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר דָּנִיֵּאל שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ כָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says Cyrus gave the vessels to Sheshbazzar, which is Daniel's name.

sources.quote: ונתנם לששבצר אשר שמהו פחת יהודה. והוא זרובבל
sources.says: Ralbag says Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah, is Zerubbabel.

sources.quote: וששבצר הוא זרובבל ולא דניאל בשתי ראיות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Sheshbazzar is Zerubbabel and not Daniel, and brings two proofs.

5:14.headline: Same letters, two words: 'his name' or 'appointed him'
5:14.body: The verse has שמה twice. Rashi reads the second one as 'his name' too, so Sheshbazzar was called Pechah, governor; Metzudat David reads it as 'whom he made governor'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נָשִׂיא וּפַחַת, וְנִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ פֶחָה
sources.says: Rashi says he was a prince and governor, and his name was called Pechah.

sources.quote: ומסרם לאיש אשר שמו ששבצר אשר עשהו למושל
sources.says: Metzudat David says Cyrus gave them to Sheshbazzar, whom he made governor.

6:4.headline: A row of wood in the wall: for strength, or for burning?
6:4.body: Every three rows of stone get one row of wood. Metzudat David says Solomon built the same way because it is stronger; Malbim brings the sages' view that the wood let the king burn it if they rebelled.

sources.quote: כי בנין כזה מחוזק ביותר וכן נאמר בבנין שלמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says this kind of building is strongest, and Solomon's was built the same way.

sources.quote: שלפי דברי חז"ל היה זה כדי שאם ימרדו ישרוף אותו באש
sources.says: Malbim brings the sages' reason: if they rebelled, the king could burn it.

sources.quote: וזה דומה לבנין ראשון, כאמרו שלשה טורי גזית וטור כרותות ארזים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this matches the first Temple: three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams.

6:11.headline: Hanged on a raised beam, or his standing walls torn down?
6:11.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read זקיף as a raised pole on which the offender is hanged. Ibn Ezra reads it as the standing walls and pillars of his house, pulled down onto the beam.

sources.quote: וְעֵץ לִתְלוֹתוֹ יְהֵא גָבוֹהַּ עָלָיו שֶׁיִּתָּלֶה עַל הָעֵץ
sources.says: Rashi says a tall beam will be set up to hang him on.

sources.quote: הוא העץ שתולין עליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the beam they hang a man on.

sources.quote: רמז לקירות ולעמודים העומדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it points to the standing walls and pillars, which will be torn down.

6:14.headline: Three kings, or one king with three names?
6:14.body: Rashi says Artaxerxes here is Darius, since every Persian king bore that title, like Pharaoh. Malbim brings both views: the sages make Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes one king, while a plain reading makes them three.

sources.quote: כִּי כָל מַלְכֵי פָרַס הָיוּ נִקְרָאִים כָּךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר כָּל מַלְכֵי מִצְרַיִם נִקְרָאִים פַּרְעֹה
sources.says: Rashi says all Persian kings were called Artaxerxes, as all Egyptian kings were called Pharaoh.

sources.quote: שלשה מלכים היו, כורש המתחיל, ודריוש המשלים בנין הבית
sources.says: Malbim quotes the plain reading: three kings, Cyrus who began, Darius who finished the house, and Artaxerxes who built the walls.

6:14.headline: God's order and the kings' orders, in one word
6:14.body: The verse uses טעם, command, both for the God of Israel and for the Persian kings. Malbim says God worked through the kings' hearts, a hidden hand rather than an open miracle.

sources.quote: שהיה השגחה מעוטפת בטבע
sources.says: Malbim says God's care was wrapped inside natural events, through the kings, not by open miracle.

6:16.headline: 'This house': a hint that another was still awaited
6:16.body: Malbim says the word 'this' points past this house. Had the people been worthy, the house Ezekiel saw would have followed, with its own dedication.

sources.quote: שמלת דנא מורה שמצפה על חנוכת בית אחר
sources.says: Malbim says the word 'this' shows they were waiting for the dedication of another house.

6:16.headline: Their joy at the dedication outshone Purim
6:16.body: Malbim says the dedication days ran into Purim, a time of feasting. The verse stresses joy because the dedication's joy was the greater one.

sources.quote: אמר שהיה עיקר החדוה על החנוכה שהיתה גדולה משמחת הפורים
sources.says: Malbim says the main joy was for the dedication, which was greater than the joy of Purim.

6:17.headline: Twelve goats for twelve tribes, though only two came back
6:17.body: The offering counts all twelve tribes. Metzudat David notes that only Judah and Benjamin returned in Second Temple times.

sources.quote: בעבור כל ישראל עם שלא חזרו בבית שני כ״א יהודה ובנימין
sources.says: Metzudat David says the goats were for all Israel, though only Judah and Benjamin returned.

6:18.headline: Two words for 'divisions': the Levites were split finer
6:18.body: Priests are set in their פלגה, Levites in their מחלקה. Malbim says the different word shows the Levites were divided further, each to his own task.

sources.quote: ועל זה אמר על הלוים במחלקותהון שהם נתחלקו יותר מן הכהנים
sources.says: Malbim says the Levites get this word because they were divided more finely than the priests.

7:7.headline: The Nethinim: 'the given ones', the Gibeonites
7:7.body: Metzudat Zion and Ralbag say the Nethinim are the Gibeonites. Ralbag explains the name: they were given (נתונים) to the service of God's house.

sources.quote: והנתינים. הגבעונים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Nethinim are the Gibeonites.

sources.quote: הם הגבעונים כי היו נתונים לעבודת בית האלהים
sources.says: Ralbag says they are the Gibeonites, called so because they were given to the service of God's house.
